original_question: Find local matching rules in dimension 2 for which the discrepancy of every tile type t in every finite tiled region R satisfies D_t(R)=|N_t(R)-d(t)vol(R)| <= c_t |∂R| for some constant c_t depending only on t.
target_in_paper: Section 2.7.2, Problem 2.7.4: Find a set of matching rules in dimension 2 satisfying condition (A) only.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target. It correctly focuses on dimension 2, on matching rules, and on Miękisz's condition (A): for each tile type t and each finite tiled region R, the discrepancy D_t(R)=|N_t(R)-d(t)vol(R)| is bounded by c_t|∂R| with c_t depending only on t. It also correctly stays with condition (A) alone, so it aligns with Problem 2.7.4 rather than the stronger Problem 2.7.3.
missing_details: The paper's official target is not an arbitrary property of tilings in dimension 2, but the existence of a set of local matching rules used to define a two-dimensional tiling (or family of admissible tilings) satisfying condition (A) only.
R should be specified exactly as a region consisting of a finite union of tiles in a tiling admitted by the matching rules.
The notation should be unpacked: N_t(R) is the number of tiles of type t in R, d(t) is the density of tile type t, and |∂R| is the measure of the boundary ∂R.

To be fully stand-alone, the question should indicate that the densities d(t) are well-defined for the tilings under consideration; the paper notes that if the system is not uniquely ergodic, fluctuations grow like volume and the problem is not relevant in that form.

It helps to state explicitly that this is condition (A) only; the separate requirement that the same bound hold for every locally admissible patch is condition (B) and belongs to Problem 2.7.3, not Problem 2.7.4.

For paper-faithful context, Problem 2.7.4 is presented as a first step toward Problem 2.7.3, and the paper notes that known 2-dimensional examples currently have discrepancy of order O(|∂R| log |∂R|), not O(|∂R|).
refined_question: Find a set of local matching rules in dimension 2, defining tilings with well-defined tile densities d(t), such that for every tile type t there exists a constant c_t depending only on t with the property that, for every region R consisting of a finite union of tiles in any tiling admitted by the rules, one has D_t(R):=|N_t(R)-d(t)vol(R)| <= c_t|∂R|, where N_t(R) is the number of tiles of type t in R and |∂R| is the measure of the boundary of R.
justification: The draft is essentially an expanded restatement of condition (A) from Section 2.7.2. Because it asks only for dimension 2 and does not include the stronger patchwise requirement in condition (B), the nearest official formulation is Problem 2.7.4, not Problem 2.7.3. The surrounding text in Section 2.7.2 defines D_t(R), N_t(R), d(t), and |∂R|, explains that the intended bound is a perimeter-order low-fluctuation estimate, notes that non-uniquely ergodic systems have volume-order fluctuations so density must be well-defined when the question is meaningful, and states that Problem 2.7.4 is a first step toward Problem 2.7.3. The same passage also records that known 2-dimensional examples such as the Penrose tiling only achieve O(|∂R| log |∂R|), which confirms that your draft is targeting the sharp open problem in the paper rather than a broader neighboring one.
